citation: Section 16(1)(n), Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 (Mah. Act No. 18 of 2000)
excerpt_text: (n) that the premises have not been used, without reasonable cause for the purpose for which they were let for for a continuous period of six months immediately preceding the date of the suit.
notes: This ground requires (i) non-use of the premises for the purpose for which they were let, (ii) without reasonable cause, and (iii) for a continuous period of six months immediately preceding the date of the suit. All three elements must be satisfied; 'without reasonable cause' is a qualifier the statute itself preserves and a court would need to assess on the facts (the text does not define what counts as reasonable cause). VERIFIED SOURCE ANOMALY: the excerpt_text's repeated word ('...they were let for for a continuous period...') is not a transcription error introduced in this KB — it is present verbatim in the official India Code primary-source PDF (text as on 7 March 2025) at this exact location. It has been preserved as-is rather than silently corrected, consistent with the rule that excerpt_text must be the exact statutory wording, typographical errors in the official text included.
applicability: Applies to a 'tenant' as defined under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999; a court-adjudicated ground under Section 16(1).
applies_to_clause_examples: Tenant must occupy the premises continuously and may not leave it vacant for any period, however brief, without cause specified.
Any vacancy of the premises by the tenant, regardless of duration, constitutes a breach entitling immediate termination.
